args.rationale: Scenario C involves fire investigator Ruth Ohanian's interview of night watchman Arno Besh, who could not speak due to smoke inhalation. When asked directly "Did you see the fan spark before the flames started?", Besh looked at her and deliberately nodded. Under the firm's rule memo (FRE 801), a nod in direct response to a question is nonverbal conduct intended as an assertion and therefore qualifies as a statement. The nod occurred out of court at the fire scene, satisfying the out-of-court element. The client letter's stated (and locked) purpose is to prove the truth of what Besh communicated by nodding — that the fan did spark before the flames. This is the truth-of-the-matter-asserted purpose. Because the nonverbal conduct qualifies as a statement under the memo's explicit treatment of nods/headshakes in response to questions, was made out of court, and is offered for the truth of its content, the item constitutes hearsay under the memo's test. Determination: hearsay — APPROVED.
